items.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

items.title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba prefix-cache hit reads out of bounds: add_request seeds the state index with cache_config.block_size after it was lowered below mamba_block_size (Xid 31 / illegal memory access)
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Summary.** `MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot as
`(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`, but by the time it runs, `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has already reassigned `cache_config.block_size` to `min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`. For hybrid models that carry an extra attention group with a small block size (here: a DFlash2/EAGLE-style drafter group with sliding-window spec, block 64 or 1024), that minimum is far below `cache_config.mamba_block_size` (7168 here). The seed therefore indexes the mamba block table in the wrong units, and `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` → `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width without a bounds check. Above the row width this is an illegal memory access (Xid 31, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`); below it, the request silently restores the KDA/mamba state from an unrelated block.

**Where.**
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`, `add_request`: `(new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size` (main, ~L70-77).
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `_initialize_kv_caches`: `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size = min(participating ...)` (main, ~L298-305). The comment there already notes that a small-block group "would otherwise drag the global block_size below the real allocator block size and desync it from mamba"; the min still includes any prefix-cacheable attention group with a smaller block.
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` uses the seed as `src_col`; `_copy_mamba_state_block` loads `block_table_base + src_col` with no check against the row width. Mamba state blocks and the block-table row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`) are in units of `mamba_block_size`.

items.title: [Bug]: HiSparse prefill can OOM a running server (unreserved host-history staging)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec, 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse, a prompt that the server accepted can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and running requests die with it. Two allocations in the HiSparse sparse-MLA prefill path aren't reserved by startup memory profiling. The profiling dummy run is one chunk of short pure prefills.

- **Full-history copy.** `stage_prefill_rows` → `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` copies the prefilling request's entire history from host into a temporary GPU buffer, one layer at a time: `(cdiv(seq_len, block_size), block_size, row_bytes)`, about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens with 576 B rows. It is freed before the next layer, so it never holds the whole KV, but it grows with prompt length and nothing reserves it.
- **Decode/prefill output join.** In mixed batches, decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens.

There are two scenarios:

1. **Prompt fits on GPU, batched with decodes** (common aggregated serving). The copy and the join are both unnecessary here, because every page is GPU-resident. They run only because of the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition in `flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`. FlashAttn and FlashInfer SM120 have the same condition, and FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill. Fixed by #60417.
2. **Prompt spilled to host**, e.g. a 1M-token prompt reaching a HiSparse decoder whose GPU can't hold its KV. The copy is required here, and its buffer is still not reserved. Fixed by #60424, which reserves a staging buffer at startup, sized for `max_model_len`.

### Repro (scenario 1)

The model is cut to 4 layers, so a 1M-token prompt fits on one B200's GPU and this exercises scenario 1, not 2.

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs

items.title: [Bug]: Sparse MLA indexer's expanded_block_table_buffer is allocated after KV sizing (1 GiB at 1M context)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ 9367d8b969, B200, Model Runner V2, DSA models (sparse MLA indexer).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The sparse MLA indexer's metadata builder allocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
self.expanded_block_table_buffer = torch.zeros(
    (scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens, block_table_width), dtype=torch.int32, ...
)
```

Builders are constructed during KV cache initialization, after available memory has been profiled and the KV cache sized. So this buffer isn't accounted for and comes out of the activation headroom.

It grows with both `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_model_len`. With the default 16384 batched tokens and `max_model_len=1048576` (block size 64), it's 16384 × 16384 × 4 B = **1 GiB** per GPU.

On 1×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers, `max_model_len=1048576`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`), persistent allocations ended up about 1.9 GiB above the planned budget, with or without HiSparse; this buffer is the largest identified piece. A long prefill then OOMed when a 2.25 GiB MoE workspace allocation couldn't fit. The same config without HiSparse failed the same way at 0.975.

Possible fixes: allocate it before memory profiling so it's counted, or size it to what the indexer actually needs. Decode token counts can in principle reach `max_num_batched_tokens`, so shrinking it needs care.

Related: #60429 (same class of bug in HiSparse, a buffer allocated after KV sizing).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Thanks to my collaborators Jianyang Gao ([@gaoj0017](https://github.com/gaoj0017)) from ETH Zurich, Peiqi Yin ([@yinpeiqi](https://github.com/yinpeiqi)) from CUHK, and Jiangneng Li ([@gravesprite](https://github.com/gravesprite)) from NTU.

### Motivation

DSA models such as **DeepSeek-V3.2/DeepSeek-V4**, **GLM-4.6/GLM-5.2**, and **LongCat-2.0** use a sparse-attention indexer during prefill. The current indexer computes an FP8 MQA score for every query/KV pair, materializes a `[num_q, seq_len]` matrix in HBM, and then runs a per-row TopK:

items.bodyExcerpt:
# Issue #49141 — Fused_moe dimension mismatch for Qwen MXFP4 model on ROCm

## 1. Root cause

The issue has two reports. Both are the same underlying defect: **a MoE layer whose
expert weights are stored *unquantized* in the checkpoint is still given a
*quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must

## Purpose

Adds an AITER-backed fusion path for the ROCm `deepseek_v32` (DeepSeek Sparse
Attention) forward, used by both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2. The existing
shared-Triton fusion path is untouched and remains the default; the AITER path
is selected at runtime per fusion via opt-in env flags, so behaviour on ROCm is
unchanged unless a flag is set.

This PR is stacked on top of: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51915, so needs enablement to land first before this fusion add-on.

### Fusions added

**1. MLA dual RMSNorm** 
Fuses the q and kv-a RMSNorms into one AITER call
(`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_out`). An out-variant was added so the norms write
model-owned buffers rather than allocating per layer, which lets the call be
hoisted out of the eager region and captured by cudagraph. Also wires the
per-token-quant variant for the quantized case.

**2. Fused QK RoPE + concat + MLA cache write** 
`rocm_aiter_fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` replaces the separate RoPE,
concat and KV-cache-write steps on the MLA path. The uint8 KV cache allocated by
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is viewed as `float8_e4m3fn` before the call, since the
AITER op rejects the raw uint8 buffer.

**3. Fused indexer QK RoPE + fp8 quant + cache write**
`rocm_aiter_indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` fuses the lightning-indexer key
LayerNorm, RoPE, fp8 quantization, and cache write into one call for the 21
indexer layers.

**4. Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm**
Uses AITER's custom all-reduce with an in-kernel RMSNorm. Gated on custom-AR
eligibility (`should_custom_ar`) because the op asserts the kernel ran, and
oversized batches must fall back to the standard path — this is the check the
torch.compile pass performs at compile time and which an inline call has to do
itself.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. # [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).
HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

## Changes

**Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse
points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Shard a GQA draft's KV by head under an MLA target
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. Mamba, CSA-linear and MLA drafts behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this. Related:

items.title: [Core] Add --release-weight-page-cache to drop checkpoint pages after load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

A DEP32 GLM-5.3 prefill group (4 pods x 8 DP ranks, DeepEP) dies as a unit: one rank stops between steps, the other 31 wait for it in `internode_dispatch`, hit the 100 s DeepEP timeout and trap (Xid 43); the stalled rank never traps. Captured on a production group right after its first real requests:

- The stalled worker's main thread was in kernel state `D` inside `__vm_munmap` for 73 s, ran for 1 s, then in a 16 KiB anonymous `mmap` (`vm_mmap_pgoff`) for 88 s. `py-spy` could not attach for exactly that window, since it needs `mmap_lock` as well.
- `perf` on the same workers under load: 1,000-3,400 `mmap` + `munmap` calls per second per worker, all 16 KiB. CPython 3.12 allocates a new frame data-stack chunk with `mmap` when a call crosses the end of the current chunk and frees it on return (python/cpython#142183, fixed in 3.13.13); the MoE forward crosses that boundary in every layer.
- The node sat at its free-memory floor for the whole stall: MemFree 16 GiB against MemAvailable 896 GiB (about 700 GiB of clean checkpoint pages plus a 761 GiB CPU KV tier in shm), with direct-reclaim bursts (`pgscan_direct` 7k-20k per 5 s), `compact_stall` 23-56 per 5 s and hundreds of `thp_fault_fallback`. MemFree jumped from 17 to 344 GiB the moment the group died.

`mmap` and `munmap` take the process `mmap_lock` for write; a page fault takes it for read and, with no free pages, holds it through direct reclaim and compaction. One faulting thread in reclaim blocks the main thread's chunk `munmap`, and the queued writer then blocks every later fault in the process, so the whole worker stops. The condition exists whenever a pod starts on a node whose previous pod left the checkpoint in the page cache (any in-place restart or rollout) and is worst on a rank's first real requests, when the KV tier faults in new pages at scale.

items.title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| | monitor off | monitor on |
|---|---|---|
| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

That's ~10 µs × ~72 calls ≈ 0.7 ms of CPU per eager step removed on GLM-5.3-Flash.

E2E, mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| this PR | 133.0 / 135.5 / 11.11 | 219.2 / 187.0 / 21.45 | 331.3 / 312.8 / 45.04 |

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip the seq_lens D2H sync in the AITER sparse MLA metadata key
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

This is the ROCm counterpart of #58684, which has the background.

On every build of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with persistent metadata (the default for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x sparse MLA), `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` runs, decode steps included. That is a blocking D2H copy, and under async scheduling it stalls the CPU until the GPU catches up. The copy only feeds the cache key that decides whether to re-run `get_mla_metadata_v1`, which was added in #42982. The metadata itself is already built on device from `paged_kv_indptr`.

The key only looks at seq_lens and context lens clamped to `index_topk`, so exact values usually aren't needed. This PR builds the key from `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` whenever that gives the same key:
- **No spec decode:** the upper bound is exact, so it's always used.
- **Spec decode:** the bound can overshoot by up to `num_speculative_tokens`. It's used once every request's `context_ub - num_speculative_tokens >= index_topk`. Past that point both lens clamp to `index_topk`, so the key is identical to the exact one. That's the steady state for long-context decode, the same regime #42982 targeted.
- **Otherwise:** it falls back to the current D2H copy.

Unlike #58684, no device fixup is needed, since AITER already plans on device.

Not changed here:
- The `synchronize()` after a metadata recompute (#47404) is untouched. The fast path never recomputes, since the key stays the same.
- Batches with any short-context request under spec decode still sync.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

**In short**: Bugfix for GLM-5.3 sometimes starting with degraded performance (thinking loops) due to dropped weights when using runai_streamer loader due to a "race" (non-deterministic I/O completion order).

**Details**:
GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) checkpoints store the indexer `wk` projection in FP8 as two tensors: values and a scale factor. The loader parks the first half in a dict and dequantizes once the second half arrives, but that dict was created fresh on every `load_weights()` call, so the two halves had to arrive within the same call.
 
With runai_streamer as loader, tensors arrive in IO-completion order (this is partly the cause for the non-deterministic "race"), and `AutoWeightsLoader` splits the weight stream into multiple `load_weights()` calls at every `model` <-> `lm_head` prefix transition. When the split between calls happens to fall between the two halves of a pair, both are silently dropped: the WK half of the fused `wk_weights_proj` parameter keeps its initialization, one layer's sparse-attention indexer runs on garbage, and every load-completeness check still passes. In production this shows up as a per-launch coin flip where short answers look fine but long reasoning degenerates into thinking loops, rendering the performance almost useless.

Fix: keep the pending dict on the model instance instead of a local variable (similar fix as #46168 for the generic `deepseek_v2` path, applied to the remaining copies: `deepseek_v32` nvidia/amd model+mtp, and `deepseek_mtp`).

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

With Model Runner V2 async scheduling and a KV output aggregator, every worker rank must send a response so the aggregator can observe connector state. The multinode worker response ring is fixed at six slots, while the async pipeline can have multiple in-flight batches. A PP8 async window has nine batches, and a batch can issue both `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` RPCs before EngineCore drains the oldest future. Workers can therefore enter the full-ring polling path during normal execution.

## Change

- Size worker response rings for `2 * max_concurrent_batches` replies.
- Keep the existing ten-slot single-node floor and six-slot multinode floor.
- Thread the multinode capacity through `GroupCoordinator.create_single_reader_mq_broadcasters` as a keyword-only argument.
- Preserve all-rank replies and KV/EC output aggregation semantics.

At PP8 with async scheduling, the multinode ring grows from 6 to 18 slots. This increases the local response-ring shared-memory reservation by 48 MiB per colocated worker (24 MiB to 72 MiB at the current 4 MiB slot size). The single-node floor remains unchanged for PP sizes where the computed window is below ten.

## Validation

### Local

- Added executor regression coverage for single-node and multinode setup, concurrent-batch windows of 2, 9, and 17, FIFO ordering, and ring wraparound.
- Candidate executor tests: 10 passed.
- Existing `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`: 29 passed, 1 skipped.
- On the same base with the new regression test and without this implementation, the 9- and 17-batch cases hit `TimeoutError` in `acquire_write`; the patched cases pass.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Rust tool parsers coerce raw parameter text by the tool's JSON schema (`tool/parameters.rs`), and argument grammars (#59395) constrain the same parameters by it, but each interpreted the schema on its own. Coercion ignored `$ref`: a parameter whose schema is `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}` came back as the JSON text string `"{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"` instead of an object. Pydantic v2 `model_json_schema()`, which most SDKs use to build tool schemas, emits exactly this for nested models, enums, and `Optional[Model]`:

```json
{"$defs": {"Place": {...}, "Unit": {"enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "type": "string"}},
 "properties": {"place": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"},
                "unit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Unit", "default": "celsius"},
                "backup": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}}}
```

This affects every schema-coercing parser: Qwen Coder and MiMo, GLM, MiniMax M2/M3, Hy. DeepSeek DSML and Kimi K3 decode by their `string=`/`type=` labels instead. Coercion and grammars also disagreed on `nullable`, `const`, single-schema `allOf`, and type-name aliases such as `"int"`, so a grammar could admit a value that the parser then decodes as another type.

The open-PR search found #50933, which resolves `$ref`/`$defs` for the Python Qwen3-Coder path; there is no Rust counterpart. Python parity is not a goal here. #59190 (the Kimi K3 full-output grammar) is stacked on this PR.

Fixes #58858

GLM-5.3-Flash serving on ROCm silently corrupts its DSA index cache. items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. - **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

items.title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- Only stage boundaries that land on a top-k-reusing layer send anything extra (`(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step). Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** `reuses_previous_topk(config, layer_id)` is factored out of the attention init.
- The model adds `topk_indices` to its intermediate tensors when any stage starts on a reusing layer.
- The receiving stage copies it into its top-k buffer.

Only the NVIDIA `deepseek_v32` model path is patched. The AMD path has the same structure and could get the same fix in a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` (sparse MLA decode) builds a
fresh runner on every call, so the trtllm-gen multi-CTA-KV kernel's semaphore

`FillFunctor<uint8>` launch before every FMHA kernel — one per layer per step —

contributing nothing but latency.

items.title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`

items.title: [ROCm][Attention] Add an mxfp4_mla KV cache for rope-free sparse MLA (read/write path)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache.

This is the first of the smaller PRs split out of #59739, as requested there. It contains only the cache format, the write path and a Triton read path. Everything is Triton or Python: no HIP or C++ sources, and no new environment variables.

## Claims

- **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token).
- **Correctness:** attention over the packed cache is bit-identical to attention over the same dequantized values stored as bf16.
- **No change for other KV dtypes.** The only shared-kernel change is a branch on the cache pointer's element type, which Triton resolves at compile time, so the bf16 and FP8 specializations compile to the same code as before.
- **No speed claim.** The Triton read path unpacks to bf16 before both dots, so it doesn't make attention faster: at 16k tokens it takes about 1.13× as long as bf16 per layer. The gain is capacity. Faster arithmetic over this cache comes in a follow-up.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X / gfx950):

```

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes scenario 2 of #60420. When a prompt's KV has spilled to host (e.g. a 1M-token prompt on a HiSparse decoder), prefill copies its history into a GPU buffer one layer at a time. Startup never reserves that buffer, so a long prompt can OOM a running server.

- Stage into the shared workspace (reserved before profiling, shared with other scratch users such as the MoE workspace), sized for one `max_model_len` request (about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens).
